constitution.title: Конституция Республики Узбекистан (принята референдумом 30 апреля 2023 года, ЗРУ-837 от 01.05.2023), консолидированная редакция
constitution.publisher: Министерство юстиции Республики Узбекистан (Национальная база данных законодательства, lex.uz)
constitution.note: Art. 9: referendums; arts. 86 and 89: Karakalpakstan's own constitution and its right to secede by a referendum of its people; art. 91: two chambers with five-year terms; art. 92: 150 deputies of the Legislative Chamber and a Senate of four members from each of Karakalpakstan, the regions, and Tashkent city, elected at joint sittings of local council deputies, plus nine appointed by the President; art. 106: President elected directly for seven years, at most two terms in a row; art. 120: Kengashes of people's deputies in regions, districts, and cities (except cities of district subordination), for five years; art. 124: khokims appointed; art. 127: citizens' assemblies elect their chairs and sit outside state power; art. 128: regular elections in the year a term expires, on the first Sunday of the third ten-day period of October; arts. 132 and 134: Constitutional and Supreme Court judges elected by the Senate.

constitution_1992.title: Конституция Республики Узбекистан от 8 декабря 1992 года (утратила силу), редакции по датам
constitution_1992.publisher: Министерство юстиции Республики Узбекистан (Национальная база данных законодательства, lex.uz)
constitution_1992.note: Original art. 77: a single-chamber Oliy Majlis of 150 deputies from territorial districts for five years (?ONDATE=08.12.1992); art. 90: President for five years, seven from the 2003 amendment; art. 77 from 2005: Legislative Chamber of 120 deputies and a Senate; art. 117 until 2021: elections on the first Sunday of the third ten-day period of December (?ONDATE=05.09.2019), moved to October by ЗРУ-670 of 8 February 2021.

classes.name: Oʻzbekiston Respublikasi Prezidenti saylovi / Выборы Президента Республики Узбекистан
classes.name_en: Presidential elections by direct vote
classes.finest_note: National totals only: the CEC's election pages give the electorate, turnout, and each candidate's votes (2000, 2007, 2015, 2016, 2023) or only percentages (2021); turnout by region appears only in infographic images.
classes.note: Direct election for seven years, at most two terms in a row (Constitution art. 106); a candidate needs more than half of the votes of those taking part, else the top two meet in a runoff within a month (Electoral Code arts. 59 and 96). Five-year terms until the 2002 referendum. Regular elections fall on the first Sunday of the third ten-day period of October of the year the term ends (art. 128), the next in 2030; the President may call an early election, as in 2023. The Supreme Soviet of the Uzbek SSR chose the first President on 24 March 1990; the first popular election was on 29 December 1991, with the independence referendum.

cadence.locator: https://lex.uz/ru/docs/111840 (art. 1: «сроком на пять лет»; art. 35: majority and runoff)
cadence.runoff_rule: More than half of the votes of those taking part, else a runoff of the top two (art. 35).
cadence.administered_by: Central Election Commission of the Republic of Uzbekistan (CEC)

cadence.locator: https://lex.uz/ru/docs/6445147 (art. 106: «сроком на семь лет»; art. 128: «в первое воскресенье третьей декады октября»)
cadence.day_rule: first Sunday of the third ten-day period of October (Constitution art. 128)
cadence.runoff_rule: More than half of the votes of those taking part wins; otherwise the two leading candidates meet within a month, no earlier than 15 days, and turnout does not count (Electoral Code arts. 59 and 96).
cadence.administered_by: Central Election Commission of the Republic of Uzbekistan (CEC)
cadence.vacancy_rule: Early election within three months when the President cannot serve, within two months when the President calls it (Electoral Code art. 66).

classes.name: Oʻzbekiston Respublikasi referendumi / Референдум Республики Узбекистан
classes.name_en: National referendums
classes.finest_note: National totals only: the CEC's 2002 page and its decision № 1245 (2023) give the electorate, turnout, and the votes for and against.
classes.note: Called by the Oliy Majlis (Referendum Law art. 13; Constitution art. 93) on the initiative of 5 percent of voters, either chamber, or the President; a proposal passes with more than half of those voting if at least half of registered voters take part (art. 38). Held on 29 December 1991 (independence), 26 March 1995 (extending the President's term to 2000), 27 January 2002 (two questions: a two-chamber parliament and a seven-year presidential term), and 30 April 2023 (the new Constitution). The 17 March 1991 Union referendum was run by the USSR while Uzbekistan was a union republic.

classes.note: 120 deputies in single-member districts in 2004; 135 districts plus 15 deputies of the Ecological Movement in 2009 and 2014; 150 districts in 2019, all needing more than half of the votes, with runoffs of the top two (Law of 1993 arts. 44-45; Electoral Code of 2019 art. 59). Since 2024, 75 districts by plurality with no runoff (arts. 9, 67, and 96); a vacated district seat gets a new election unless within six months of the term's end (art. 74). No by-election has been held since 2019. The chamber's 2019 regular date was the first Sunday of the third ten-day period of December; October from 2021.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes votes by district: the CEC's pages give national turnout and seat totals, and its 2024 decision lists only each district's winner; district election commissions' protocols are not published.

cadence.locator: https://lex.uz/ru/docs/35869?ONDATE=05.09.2019%2000 (art. 117: «в первое воскресенье третьей декады декабря»); Electoral Code of 2019 arts. 59, 67, and 96
cadence.day_rule: first Sunday of the third ten-day period of December (Constitution of 1992 art. 117)
cadence.runoff_rule: More than half of the votes of those taking part; otherwise the top two meet in a repeat vote within a month.
cadence.administered_by: Central Election Commission of the Republic of Uzbekistan (CEC)

cadence.vacancy_rule: New election in the district, unless the vacancy falls within six months of the end of the term (Electoral Code art. 74).

classes.name: Oʻzbekiston Respublikasi Oliy Majlisiga saylov (bir palatali) / Выборы в Олий Мажлис (однопалатный)
classes.name_en: Oliy Majlis (single chamber, 250 seats), 1994-2004
classes.note: 250 deputies in single-member districts for five years, needing more than half of the votes with runoffs (Law of 28 December 1993 № 990-XII); elected 25 December 1994 with further rounds on 8 and 22 January 1995, and 5 December 1999 with runoffs on 19 December. Replaced by the two-chamber Oliy Majlis after the 2002 referendum.
classes.disposition_reason: No district results are published by an official body: the CEC's site gives only a national prose summary of 1999 and nothing for 1994-1995, and the parliament's histories give seat totals by party.

classes.name: Oʻzbekiston SSR Oliy Soveti / Oliy Kengash
classes.name_en: Supreme Soviet of the Uzbek SSR (from 1991 the Oliy Kengash of the Republic of Uzbekistan), 1938-1994
classes.note: Single-candidate district elections under the 1937 and 1978 constitutions of the Uzbek SSR until the competitive election of 1990, whose Supreme Soviet declared independence on 31 August 1991, adopted the 1992 Constitution as the Oliy Kengash, and called the first Oliy Majlis election for 25 December 1994.
classes.disposition_reason: Results were printed only in the official press of the time; no current official body publishes them, and the CEC's records begin in 1999.

classes.name: Oliy Majlis Senati aʼzolari saylovi / Выборы членов Сената Олий Мажлиса
classes.name_en: Senate members elected at joint sittings of local council deputies, 2005-
classes.note: Each of the 14 units (Karakalpakstan, 12 regions, Tashkent city) elects senators by secret ballot at a joint sitting of the deputies of its Jokargy Kenes or regional, district, and city Kengashes, within a month of the local elections, under the CEC: six each (84) until 2023, four each (56) since (Constitution art. 92; Electoral Code arts. 75-87). Joint sittings were held in January 2005, 2010, 2015, and 2020 and on 7-12 November 2024; vacancies are filled at further joint sittings.
classes.disposition_reason: The CEC registers the elected senators by region (decisions № 1023 of 2020 and № 1420 of 2024) but publishes no candidates' votes from the joint sittings.

access.license: Attribution to www.saylov.uz required; all rights reserved (site footer)
access.evidence: Decision № 1420 attaches the list of senators elected from each region, with no votes.

cadence.runoff_rule: Repeat voting at the same joint sitting, then repeat elections (Electoral Code arts. 83-84).
cadence.administered_by: Central Election Commission of the Republic of Uzbekistan (CEC)

dates.note: Joint sittings of January 2005, 2010, and 2015 (84 senators each); not on the CEC's site.

classes.disposition_reason: Appointed by the President from distinguished citizens, with no vote.

classes.name: Oʻzbekiston Ekologik harakatidan saylanadigan deputatlar / Депутаты от Экологического движения Узбекистана
classes.name_en: Legislative Chamber deputies chosen by the Ecological Movement of Uzbekistan, 2009-2019
classes.locator: https://lex.uz/ru/docs/71045 (art. 1: «Пятнадцать депутатов ... избираются от Экологического движения Узбекистана»)
classes.disposition_reason: The 15 deputies were chosen at a conference of the movement on election day, not by voters; the Electoral Code of 2019 ended the reserved seats.

classes.name: Oliy Majlis va Kengashlar tomonidan saylanadigan mansabdor shaxslar / Должностные лица, избираемые палатами и Кенгашами
classes.name_en: Officers chosen by elected bodies (chamber speakers, Kengash chairs, the CEC, and the Constitutional and Supreme Court judges elected by the Senate)
classes.disposition_reason: Votes inside elected bodies, part of their proceedings rather than elections run by the CEC.

classes.name: Sudyalar / Судьи
classes.name_en: Judges
classes.disposition_reason: Judges are elected by the Senate or appointed by the President on the Supreme Judicial Council's proposal, never by voters.

classes.name: Siyosiy partiyalar tomonidan nomzod koʻrsatish / Выдвижение кандидатов политическими партиями
classes.name_en: Party nominations of candidates
classes.disposition_reason: Parties nominate candidates at their own congresses and plenums; the state runs no nominating contest.

classes.name: Qaraqalpaqstan Respublikası Joqarğı Keңesine saylaw / Выборы в Жокаргы Кенес Республики Каракалпакстан
classes.name_en: Jokargy Kenes (Supreme Council) of the Republic of Karakalpakstan
classes.finest_note: No results are published centrally; the infographic of the CEC gives only the number of deputies.
classes.note: 65 deputies in single-member districts for five years, needing more than half of the votes with 33 percent turnout, else a runoff (Karakalpakstan Law «О выборах» of 2019, arts. 9, 59, 61, and 77), run by the Central Election Commission of Karakalpakstan on the same day as the Legislative Chamber.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes votes by district or the elected list online: the Karakalpak election commission has no results pages on saylov.uz, and the CEC gives only the size of the body.

cadence.administered_by: Central Election Commission of the Republic of Karakalpakstan

dates.note: Elected with the Oliy Majlis and the Legislative Chamber in 1994, 1999, 2004, 2009, 2014, and 2019; not published online.

classes.name: Qaraqalpaqstan xalqınıń ulıwma referendumı / Всеобщий референдум народа Каракалпакстана
classes.name_en: Referendums of the people of Karakalpakstan
classes.note: The Constitution gives Karakalpakstan the right to secede by a general referendum of its people (art. 89); none has been held.

classes.name: Viloyat va Toshkent shahar xalq deputatlari Kengashlariga saylov / Выборы в областные и Ташкентский городской Кенгаши народных депутатов
classes.name_en: Regional and Tashkent city Kengashes of people's deputies
classes.finest_note: Election commissions of the regions publish scanned lists of the winners per district (Tashkent city, 2024), with no votes; the CEC publishes nothing by council.
classes.note: Elected in territorial single-member districts on a multi-party basis for five years, on the same day as the Legislative Chamber (Electoral Code art. 88; Constitution art. 120); a majority with runoffs until 2023, plurality since. Vacated seats get by-elections called by the CEC, skipped within six months of the term's end (art. 93). Each has 30 to 60 deputies by population. Tashkent city's Kengash had 50 districts in 2024.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes votes for local Kengash districts: the CEC gives only national composition figures, and the regional commissions' decisions list winners without votes as scanned PDFs.

cadence.vacancy_rule: New election in the district, unless within six months of the end of the term (Electoral Code art. 93).

classes.name: Oʻzbekiston SSR mahalliy xalq deputatlari Sovetlari / Местные Советы народных депутатов Узбекской ССР
classes.name_en: Local soviets of people's deputies of the Uzbek SSR (regional, district, city, settlement, and village), to 1994
classes.note: Elected in single-member districts under the constitutions of the Uzbek SSR, last in 1990, until the 1994 law replaced them with Kengashes of people's deputies in regions, districts, and cities.
classes.disposition_reason: Results were printed only in the official press of the time; no current official body publishes them.

classes.name: Hokimlar / Хокимы
classes.name_en: Khokims (heads of regions, Tashkent city, districts, and cities)
classes.disposition_reason: Appointed for five years by the President (regions and Tashkent city) or by the regional khokim with the Kengash's approval (districts and cities), never elected by voters.

classes.name: Fuqarolar yigʻini raisi saylovi / Выборы председателя схода граждан
classes.name_en: Chairs (aksakals) of citizens' assemblies (mahallas, towns, kishlaks, and auls)
classes.note: Each assembly elects its chair for five years by secret ballot at a meeting of residents or, where one cannot be convened, of their representatives, on dates set by the Jokargy Kenes and the regional and Tashkent city Kengashes, with commissions of assistance rather than the CEC (Law № ЗРУ-499 arts. 8, 10, 12, and 20).
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen at meetings of residents or their representatives, outside the Electoral Code and the CEC, for bodies the Constitution places outside state power (art. 127); no official body publishes the votes.
